Final categorization: POSSIBLE  
(Justification: This is a non-review research paper that uses future land-use change scenarios derived from Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) as an input layer to refine pest risk projections for Thrips palmi under climate change. The primary objective is not LULC prediction itself; rather, LULC projections (specifically agricultural area extent under SSP1, SSP2, and SSP3) are used as a filter to assess invasion risk in agriculturally suitable areas. The LULC scenarios were developed by Kim (2016) and applied here without the authors generating new LULC models or validating LULC accuracy. While the study covers the entire Korean peninsula (national scale), implements ≥2 future scenarios (three SSPs combined with two RCPs), and includes mapped outputs, LULC prediction is not the central focus—it serves as a contextual constraint in an ecological niche modeling study. Thus, it meets inclusion criteria for national scale and multi-scenario use but fails the “primary focus = LULC prediction” requirement, placing it in 'POSSIBLE'. It does not meet any exclusion criteria, as it is species-focused but explicitly integrates spatially explicit LULC data.)
